scenes.tts: He found the most important fold in biology flat on his back, with a sinus infection and a sheet of paper. No lab, no model kit — just a chain he refused to force closed after a whole number of residues, the way everyone else had assumed it must.
scenes.visual: chain that stays open: sinus infection, paper, no lab, chain not closed after a whole number
scenes.narration: He found the most important fold in biology flat on his back, with a sinus infection and a sheet of paper. No lab, no model kit — just a chain he refused to force closed after a whole number of residues, the way everyone else had assumed it must.

scenes.tts: Folding the paper at roughly the right bond angles, he let the geometry decide.
scenes.visual: paper folded at the right bond angles; the geometry decides
scenes.narration: Folding the paper at roughly the right bond angles, he let the geometry decide.

scenes.tts: What fell out was untidy on purpose: a right-handed helix that came around every 3.6 residues, rising 5.4 Ångströms per turn, with each carbonyl oxygen reaching up the axis to clasp the amide hydrogen four residues along, a regular ladder of hydrogen bonds running parallel to the helix axis.
scenes.visual: side-view tile helix: right-handed, 3.6 per turn, 5.4 A rise, CO to NH four along, ladder parallel to axis
scenes.narration: What fell out was untidy on purpose: a right-handed helix that came around every 3.6 residues, rising 5.4 Ångströms per turn, with each carbonyl oxygen reaching up the axis to clasp the amide hydrogen four residues along, a regular ladder of hydrogen bonds running parallel to the helix axis.

scenes.tts: He had read the structure off the bonding, the way he read everything. He called it the alpha helix, and he could not let it go: "I was so pleased with this structure that I stayed up until late in the night, pondering about it," he recalled.
scenes.visual: read off the bonding; alpha helix; could not let it go

scenes.tts: Experiment confirmed it only later. The geometry had been enough.
